background_rationale: After starting as a bank programmer, he spent nearly two decades in Cisco's sales organization, rising from account manager to head of worldwide field operations before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: Cisco announced it would cut about 4,250 jobs, roughly 5% of its workforce, as Robbins cited customer caution and weak demand from telecom and cable providers.
Cisco completed its acquisition of Splunk for about $28 billion in equity value, the largest acquisition in the company's history.
Robbins told Fortune he expected companies to stop talking about corporate social responsibility as a separate activity, saying people now understand the underlying business value of diversity.
Cisco reported record fiscal 2026 revenue of $63.3 billion, up 12%, with $9.3 billion in AI-infrastructure orders; Robbins said Cisco is well positioned to support customers wherever they deploy AI.

personal_story.hook: Chuck Robbins began as a bank programmer and joined Cisco's sales team in 1997; he has led the company since 2015.
personal_story.summary: Robbins was born in Grayson, Georgia, and graduated from Rocky Mount High School in North Carolina before earning a mathematics degree with a computer science concentration at UNC-Chapel Hill in 1987. He began his career as an application developer at North Carolina National Bank, then moved into networking at Wellfleet, Bay Networks and Ascend. He joined Cisco in 1997 as an account manager and rose through its sales organization to run worldwide field operations. When he was named to succeed longtime CEO John Chambers in 2015, he said he planned to spend his first 90 days listening.
